title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Bacterial Genetics
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 4 · 9 questions · 78 marks · 24 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a quarter · every question is an actual exam paper question
los_html:
Learning outcomes, against the questions that test them.
1(a) the cell theory: the three statements, in the outcome's own wordsQ8
1(d) the structure of a typical bacterial cell: the five named featuresQ1(a), Q1(c), Q2(c), Q3, Q8
2(d) the bacterial chromosome and the nucleoidQ1(b), Q1(c), Q2(a), Q2(b), Q9(c)
2(d) packing of prokaryotic DNA: histone-like proteins, looped domains, supercoilingQ1(b), Q2(b)
2(d) plasmids as extrachromosomal DNAQ1(a), Q1(c), Q2(b), Q7(a), Q9(c)
2(d) prokaryotic against eukaryotic genome, on the outcome's own axesQ2(a), Q2(b)
2(d) endosymbiont evidence: circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, division by splitting, own machineryQ2(c)
2(g) binary fission, outlined step by stepQ3, Q4(a), Q9(c)
2(g) why binary fission cannot generate variation, and what it can still doQ4(a), Q4(b), Q7(c)
2(g) vertical against horizontal gene transferQ4(c), Q4(d), Q9(a), Q9(b), Q9(c)
2(g) transformation: naked DNA, competent cells, competence factorsQ5(a), Q5(b), Q6(a), Q9(a)
2(g) transduction, generalised and specialised, and the phage that pairs with eachQ5(c), Q6(b), Q7(b), Q9(a), Q9(c)
2(g) conjugation: F plasmid, sex pilus, mating bridge, oriT, rolling circleQ7(a), Q7(b), Q9(a), Q9(c)
2(g) homologous recombination, and why conjugation is the exceptionQ6(b), Q7(b)
2(g) why variation matters: gaining genes, selection pressure, antibiotic resistanceQ7(c), Q9(a)
1(f) how viruses challenge the cell theory (cumulative from Cluster 1)Q8
reach-back Cluster 1: the viral genome, the lytic and lysogenic cycles, the prophageQ2(d), Q5(c), Q6(b), Q7(b), Q8
reach-back Book 2: histones, nucleosomes, introns, splicing, semi-conservative replicationQ2(b), Q3, Q9(c)
reach-back Book 3: mitosis, the spindle, the nuclear envelope, meiosis and fertilisationQ3, Q8

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required ANSWERS and not just for duplicated labels. Q1 the bacterial cell described on the axes the outcome names · Q2 the specimen's own genome comparison, plus where mitochondria came from · Q3 binary fission end to end against mitosis · Q4 what binary fission can and cannot do, argued from a real culture · Q5 the three mechanisms used as hypotheses to be eliminated · Q6 transformation's preconditions and the two transduction accidents · Q7 the F plasmid, and the two structures that are not the same structure · Q8 the cell theory argued three ways at once · Q9 what each process actually moves. Two shared points are declared rather than hidden. Q7(a) and Q7(b) both credit the sex pilus followed by the mating bridge, but (a) is otherwise about tra genes, oriT and the rolling circle while (b) is otherwise about vectors, contact and homologous recombination. Q7(b) and Q9(c) both identify what conjugation and transduction transfer, but (b) marks it as a five-axis contrast and (c) marks it as a per-row audit of a table. Every other pair was checked at the level of the paragraph the scheme demands, and no two need the same one.
